cards.explanation: The answer is every firstborn male. The LORD tells Moses, Israel's leader, “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male.” (Exodus 13:2) It covers the firstborn from every womb among the Israelites, man and beast. Clear instructions, friends. I wish my recipes came that clear.

The answer is False, and the text says so outright. The LORD says the firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Him, “…both of man and beast.” (Exodus 13:2) Animals are in it, not just people. Nobody gets left off this list.

The answer is the day they came out of Egypt. Moses tells the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand.” (Exodus 13:3) It's a day worth remembering, friends. The reason is right there in the verse: the LORD's hand brought them out.

The answer is in the land He swore to their fathers. Moses says that when the LORD brings them into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites and Jebusites, “…the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you…” they will keep this service in this month (Exodus 13:5). So it's a promise they're walking toward. They haven't arrived yet.

The two answers are seven and feast. Moses says, “For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread…” (Exodus 13:6) That's a commitment, friends, and I respect a long bake. Then on the seventh day, Moses says, “…there shall be a feast to the LORD.” (Exodus 13:6) That's the kind of ending I like: you work all week, then you get a party.

The answer is False. It's bigger than the houses. Moses says, “Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.” (Exodus 13:7) Anywhere within their borders, friends. That's a lot of ground to cover.

The answer is to explain what the LORD did for them. Moses says, “And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’” (Exodus 13:8) The feast comes with a story attached. The telling is part of the day.

The answer is False, because the feast keeps coming back. Moses says, “Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.” (Exodus 13:10) Same time every year, friends. It's a standing date on the calendar.
The answer is a lamb. Moses says, “You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb…” (Exodus 13:13) So the donkey is bought back, and a lamb is the price. It's a straight swap.

The answer is False. They don't keep it to work the land. Moses says, “…if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck.” (Exodus 13:13) It's a heavy line, friends, and the text doesn't soften it. So the choice is redeem it with a lamb, or that.

The answer is because the LORD killed Egypt's firstborn, and it's a heavy one. Moses says, “…when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast.” (Exodus 13:15) Pharaoh was Egypt's king. That's why the Israelites sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but redeem all the firstborn of their sons.

The answer is that they might face war and turn back. God says, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.” (Exodus 13:17) The road through the land of the Philistines was shorter, friends, and He still steered them off it. Think of someone who quits a job on a Friday, then spends the whole weekend wanting to call the boss and take it back. War could do that to a crowd of people who had just left slavery.

The answer is through the wilderness toward the Red Sea. “So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea.” (Exodus 13:18) Notice the word "around," friends: it's the long way, and it's the way God picked. I once took the scenic way across the counter and ended up in a pile of flour. Here the text says God is the One leading, and the people left Egypt "…arrayed for battle."

The answer is True. “…the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.” (Exodus 13:18) They're walking out of the house of slavery, friends, and they're arrayed for battle. If it were me, I'd show up with a rolling pin and a big mustache. That's the verse's picture of them as they leave, and it's right in the same verse where God leads them the long way around.

The answer is the bones of Joseph. “Moses took the bones of Joseph with him…” (Exodus 13:19) Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, “…you must carry my bones with you from this place.” So Moses carries them out of Egypt. That's a promise getting kept.

The answer is that Joseph made the sons of Israel swear. Moses took Joseph's bones “…because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath…” (Exodus 13:19) It was a promise, friends, and they kept it. A solemn oath is no small thing.

The answer is a pillar of cloud. “And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day…” (Exodus 13:21) By night He goes before them in a pillar of fire to give them light. Neither pillar left its place before the people (Exodus 13:22). Day or night, they could travel.

The answer is fire. The LORD went before them “…in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.” (Exodus 13:21) Cloud by day, fire by night, friends. That's how they can keep going.

The answer is False, because it stays put. “Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.” (Exodus 13:22) Day or night, it's there in front of them. No trip where they have to wonder where it went.
